high.title: Peso to Stay at P61 Level as War Continues
high.summary: The Philippine peso closed the week at P61.29/USD on Friday, flat on the day but down 51.5 centavos week-on-week from its P60.775 close on June 19. Market participants described trading as range-bound within P61.20–P61.36, citing a lack of fresh domestic catalysts. The primary driver of peso weakness remains elevated geopolitical risk stemming from the ongoing US-Iran conflict, now entering its fourth month with no clear resolution in sight. Trader caution is keeping the peso on the defensive, and the outlook for the coming week is sideways consolidation at the P61 handle. For FX traders, the key watch points are any breakthrough or escalation in Middle East peace negotiations, which could trigger a directional break from the current range. USD demand from risk-off positioning continues to cap peso recovery attempts. Until geopolitical visibility improves, expect the peso to remain under modest depreciation pressure, with the P61.50 level serving as the next meaningful resistance zone to monitor.

high.title: Debt Yields End Mixed on Fragile US-Iran Peace Deal
high.summary: Philippine government securities (GS) yields ended mixed last week, rising by a modest average of 0.36 basis points week-on-week, according to PHP Bloomberg Valuation Service (BVAL) Reference Rates as of June 26. The short end of the curve saw yields move mostly higher, reflecting dual pressures: uncertainty surrounding fragile US-Iran ceasefire negotiations and incoming US inflation data that has reignited speculation around Federal Reserve rate hikes. A renewed Fed tightening cycle would be materially negative for PHP bonds, as it would widen the rate differential in favor of the USD, amplifying peso depreciation pressure and potentially forcing the BSP into a defensive policy stance. Bond investors should closely watch upcoming US CPI/PCE releases and any Fed communication for signals on the rate path. Domestically, the mixed yield movement suggests the market lacks a decisive directional bias, with geopolitical risk and external monetary policy uncertainty serving as the dominant overhangs. The fragility of any US-Iran deal remains the key wildcard for global risk sentiment and, by extension, Philippine bond demand.

high.title: BSP Securities' Average Rate Rises Despite Strong Demand
high.summary: The BSP's 28-day bills attracted exceptionally strong demand at Friday's auction, with total tenders reaching P85.659 billion — nearly triple the P30 billion on offer — versus P70.215 billion in tenders at the prior June 19 auction. The bid-to-cover ratio surged to 2.8553x from 2.3405x previously, signaling robust appetite for short-term BSP paper. Notably, the average yield rose despite the oversubscription, suggesting that while demand is high, bidders are pricing in a slightly higher rate environment, possibly reflecting the same US inflation and geopolitical risks weighing on the broader GS market. The BSP fully awarded the offering. For monetary policy watchers, the rising average rate on BSP bills — even amid strong demand — is an important signal: the market may be gently testing the BSP's tolerance for short-end rate drift. This has implications for the overnight reverse repurchase rate outlook and overall liquidity management. Bond traders should monitor whether this trend of rising BSP bill yields persists in upcoming auctions, as it could foreshadow a shift in the short-end yield curve and influence the BSP's next policy move.

high.title: BSP Sees Wider Balance of Payments Gap Until 2027
high.summary:
The BSP has revised its BoP deficit forecast significantly wider, now projecting a **$10.7 billion deficit (-2.1% of GDP)** for 2026, deteriorating further through 2027. The revision is attributed to weak global trade conditions and tighter external financing conditions weighing on the Philippines' external position. This is a materially bearish development for the **Philippine Peso (PHP)**, as a widening BoP deficit signals persistent net foreign exchange outflows, reducing the BSP's ability to defend the currency without drawing down gross international reserves (GIR). For **bond investors**, a deteriorating external position raises sovereign risk perceptions and could push foreign holders to reduce PHP-denominated government bond exposure, pressuring yields higher. FX traders should watch for BSP intervention signals and any acceleration in GIR drawdowns. The trajectory toward 2027 suggests this is not a transient shock — medium-term PHP weakness is a credible base case. **Key risk: further escalation in the Middle East could worsen the current account via higher oil import bills, compounding the deficit.**

high.title: Yields on Short-Term Gov't Debt End Higher on Hawkish BSP, Fed
high.summary: The Bureau of the Treasury (BTr) fully awarded P90 billion in short-term government securities — comprising Cash Management Bills (CMBs) and Treasury bills (T-bills) — with total tenders reaching P178.888 billion, slightly below the prior auction's P180.7 billion. Yields ended mostly higher, driven by dual hawkish signals from both the BSP and the US Federal Reserve, compounded by ongoing uncertainty from the unresolved Middle East conflict. The strong bid-to-cover ratio confirms solid domestic demand for short-dated paper, but the upward yield drift signals the market is pricing in a more restrictive monetary policy path. For bond investors, this reinforces a cautious duration stance — particularly on the short end, which is most sensitive to policy rate expectations. The hawkish BSP posture, corroborated by S&P's forecast (see below), suggests the yield curve may face further upward pressure in H2 2026. Traders should watch the next BTr auction for continued yield creep and monitor BSP communication for any shift in forward guidance.

high.title: S&P Expects One More BSP Rate Increase This Year
high.summary: S&P Global Ratings has explicitly forecast that the BSP will deliver one additional 25bps rate hike in 2026, bringing the policy rate to 5.00% by year-end. S&P Senior Asia-Pacific Economist Vishrut Rana flagged that while the tightening is modest, it carries a medium-term risk of weighing on domestic demand. This is a high-conviction signal for markets: the terminal rate narrative is now anchored at 5%, which has direct implications for the entire Philippine government bond yield curve, PHP carry dynamics, and credit conditions in the banking sector. For FX traders, a higher-for-longer BSP rate supports PHP on the carry side but may dampen growth expectations, creating a mixed medium-term outlook. Bond investors should reassess duration positioning — particularly in the 2–5 year segment — as the market recalibrates to a 5% terminal rate. The key risk event to watch is the next BSP Monetary Board meeting for timing confirmation of this anticipated hike.

medium.title: GS Rates to Track Secondary Market
medium.summary: The Bureau of the Treasury (BTr) is set to auction up to P90 billion in short-term government securities this week, comprising P30 billion in Cash Management Bills (P20 billion in 35-day and P10 billion in 63-day instruments) and P60 billion in Treasury bills. Auction yields are expected to track secondary market movements and may end mixed, with fresh volatility introduced by stalled US-Iran negotiations. For bond market participants, this is a significant weekly supply event at the short end of the curve. Given the mixed yield environment and geopolitical uncertainty flagged in the secondary market, demand will be a key indicator of investor risk appetite. Traders should watch auction results closely for cut-off rate direction and bid-to-cover ratios as a gauge of near-term market sentiment on Philippine short-term rates.

medium.title: BIS Warns Debt, AI Boom and Financial Fragilities Raise Global Risks
medium.summary: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) Annual Economic Report has flagged a complex set of global vulnerabilities, including rising public debt, financial system fragilities, supply shock risks, and the sustainability of the AI investment boom, all of which could contribute to a renewed bout of stubbornly high inflation globally. For Philippine markets, this macro backdrop is relevant as a tighter-for-longer global rate environment — driven by persistent inflation — would sustain USD strength, pressure the peso, and keep Philippine bond yields elevated. The BIS's call for disciplined policymaking reinforces the case for the BSP to maintain a cautious monetary stance. Fund managers with PHP exposure should factor in these global risk factors as a medium-term headwind for emerging market assets, including the peso and Philippine fixed income.

medium.title: Analysts Say Lower Philippine Growth Goals More Realistic
medium.summary: The DBCC has slashed its 2026 GDP growth target to **3.5%-4.5%** from the prior **5%-6%**, with analysts broadly endorsing the revision as more reflective of ground realities. Elevated inflation and sluggish consumer demand are cited as persistent downside risks, alongside potential Middle East conflict escalation. For PHP and rates markets, slower growth reduces the urgency for the BSP to tighten monetary policy, tilting the bias toward further easing — which is marginally **PHP-negative** but **supportive of government bonds** if rate cuts materialize. Weaker growth also implies softer fiscal revenues, which could pressure the government's borrowing program and bond supply dynamics. Fund managers should reassess growth-sensitive PSEi sector exposures given the materially lower trajectory.

medium.title: Stocks to Trade Sideways as Risks Cloud Outlook
medium.summary: The **PSEi closed at 6,072.24**, up a negligible 0.01% on Friday, but posted a **week-on-week decline of 63.11 points** from 6,135.35, failing to reclaim the key 6,150 resistance level. Analysts expect continued sideways trading as inflationary pressures from the Middle East conflict and broader macroeconomic uncertainty weigh on sentiment. The inability to hold above 6,150 is technically bearish in the near term, suggesting limited upside catalysts. For equity-focused fund managers, risk/reward remains unfavorable until geopolitical risks abate and domestic growth data stabilizes. The confluence of BoP deterioration and lower growth targets (see above) reinforces a **cautious near-term stance on PSEi**.

medium.title: High Power Costs and Corruption Scandal to Affect PHL Role in Global Supply Chain
medium.summary: UK-based risk intelligence firm **Verisk Maplecroft** warns that the Philippines risks losing competitiveness in global supply chain realignment due to **high energy costs** (exacerbated by the Hormuz crisis) and unresolved corruption issues tied to infrastructure projects. This has negative implications for **foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows**, a key support for the PHP and the capital account. Deteriorating investor sentiment — if sustained — could further widen the BoP deficit identified above, compounding PHP headwinds. FX and equity investors should monitor whether the government moves decisively to address these structural concerns, as inaction could deter the FDI flows needed to offset the current account deficit.

medium.title: Peso Climbs with US, Iran Set to Resume Talks
medium.summary: The Philippine peso appreciated 12 centavos on Monday, closing at P61.17 per dollar from P61.29 on Friday, after the US and Iran agreed to halt hostilities and resume peace negotiations — reducing geopolitical risk sentiment that had been weighing on emerging market currencies. Intraday, the peso ranged between P61.32 (low) and P61.125 (best level), suggesting a measured but meaningful risk-on move rather than a sharp reversal. For FX traders, the P61.00–P61.30 range is the near-term corridor to watch; further de-escalation in the Middle East could push PHP toward the stronger end, while any resumption of tensions would likely push it back above P61.30. The Middle East conflict remains a key macro overhang for PHP given its impact on oil prices, OFW remittance flows from the region, and broader global risk appetite.

medium.title: World Bank Approves $1.02-B Loan for Philippine Energy Transition and Water Security
medium.summary: The World Bank approved a $1.02-billion Development Policy Loan (DPL) to the Philippines, comprising a $1-billion IBRD facility and a $20-million concessional tranche, targeting clean energy deployment, electricity market reforms, and water management improvements. From a capital flows and balance of payments perspective, this represents a significant official sector inflow that provides modest but positive support to Philippine foreign reserves and the peso. While not a direct FX market mover, multilateral loan disbursements of this scale contribute to external financing buffers and reduce sovereign refinancing risk. Bond investors may view this positively as it signals continued multilateral confidence in the Philippine reform agenda, marginally supportive of sovereign credit spreads.

medium.title: PSE Index Rises on IPO News, Easing US-Iran Woes
medium.summary:
The PSEi gained 1.0% (+61.17 points) to close at 6,133.41, reclaiming the 6,100 level, while the broader All Shares Index rose 0.67% to 3,352.96. The rally was driven by two catalysts: easing US-Iran geopolitical tensions, which improved global risk appetite, and fresh IPO pipeline developments that renewed domestic investor optimism. For equity and FX traders, a sustained PSEi recovery above 6,100 could attract incremental foreign portfolio inflows, providing modest support to the PHP. Watch for whether foreign buying participation accompanies this move — net foreign buying would be a constructive signal for both the PSEi and the peso. The IPO-driven sentiment is a domestic tailwind worth monitoring for near-term momentum.
